subject: general
question:
The statement below has been given with bracketed text. Select the option with correct idiom for the bracketed text.

That new budget bill was (totally useless) before it hit the Senate.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'** i.e. **'A dead duck'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct idiom to substitute for the bracketed text **"totally useless"** is: **'A dead duck'**
 
• **"A dead duck"** is an idiom used to describe something that is ineffective, useless, or doomed to failure, which matches with the meaning of **"totally useless"** in the context of the sentence.(असफल होना या असफल होने वाला)

Therefore, the** correct answer** is correct:** 'A dead duck'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Now let's explain all the given options along with their English and Hindi meanings:
 
 
• **"A cry wolf":** This idiom is based on the story of the Boy Who Cried Wolf and is used to refer to someone who raises false alarms, i.e., giving false warnings or claims.(झूठी चेतावनी देना)
 
• **"Cold feet":** This idiom refers to nervousness or fear that prevents you from completing an action. (डर या घबराहट होना)
 
• **"A fuel to the fire":** This idiom means to worsen an already bad situation.(आग में घी डालना)
